scope: Default flat-ground Ant-v5 simulation only; exploratory mechanism pilot.
research_question: Do bounded forward-velocity tracking and a policy action-rate penalty reduce hopping and action roughness without destroying commanded forward locomotion?
design: Two-by-two factorial mechanism screen. All non-focal reward, environment and PPO settings are held fixed.

action_rate_penalty.weight_rationale: At the previously observed proposed roughness near 0.2-0.3, weight 0.2 contributes approximately -0.04 to -0.06 per step: material but smaller than the +1 healthy term.

velocity_tracking_reward.rationale: The target matches the centre of the frozen 0.8-1.2 m/s intent interval; the reward is maximal at the command and removes unbounded incentive for faster hopping.

observation.rationale: All policies observe the prior action, so the action-rate objective is Markov and comparator observations remain identical.

constraint.rationale: The external slew projector is disabled so this pilot measures learned policy smoothness rather than mechanically filtered actions.

seed_role: New development seeds not used in the preceding hybrid-guardrail rounds; not reserved formal seeds.
stopping_rule: Complete the frozen 12-policy matrix. Do not tune the two candidate weights from its outcomes; use results only to choose the next predeclared mechanism question.
claim_boundary: Development mechanism evidence only; no formal mitigation, natural-gait or real-robot claim.
